sources.title: Farm practices survey February 2026
facts: Defra reports 2026 England farm-practice survey results across nutrient management, anaerobic digestion, emissions, manure/slurry, grassland and livestock practices.
Survey adoption and responses are not direct farm or parcel greenhouse-gas measurements.

sources.title: Farm practices survey February 2026 introduction
facts: The introduction summarises headline 2026 practice adoption results.
Headline proportions are England survey estimates and not census or parcel observations.

sources.title: Farm practices survey February 2026 metadata
facts: The survey targeted about 7,000 holdings and reports an approximately 22 percent voluntary response rate.
Sampling thresholds and response weighting must be retained when interpreting practice proportions.

sources.title: Farm practices survey 2026 emissions
facts: Defra reports farmer attitudes and actions intended to reduce GHG emissions, including energy efficiency and manure-management actions.
Taking an action or reporting its adoption is not measured emissions reduction.

sources.title: Farm practices survey 2026 nutrient management
facts: The release reports nutrient plans, testing and whole-farm nutrient-balance practices.
A plan, soil test or nutrient balance is an activity/management indicator rather than a direct N2O or parcel GHG measurement.

sources.title: Farm practices survey 2026 anaerobic digestion
facts: The release reports the proportion of holdings processing waste, crops or feedstocks by anaerobic digestion.
AD adoption and feedstock use do not by themselves quantify methane capture, leakage or avoided emissions.

sources.title: Farm practices survey 2026 fertiliser manure and slurry spreaders
facts: The release reports spreading responsibilities and spreader calibration practices.
Spreader use/calibration is mitigation-practice evidence and not measured N2O or ammonia-to-GHG conversion.

sources.title: Farm practices survey 2026 manure and slurry storage
facts: The release reports manure and slurry storage types, cover status, capacity and planned upgrades.
Storage configuration can affect emissions but does not directly measure methane or nitrous-oxide release.

sources.title: Farm practices survey 2026 grassland and grazing
facts: The release reports clover/high-sugar grass, reseeding and grazing-management practices.
Practice adoption and agronomic potential are not measured soil carbon or parcel GHG change.

sources.title: Farm practices survey 2026 livestock feeding regimes and breeding practices
facts: The release reports ration formulation, forage and breeding practices linked to productivity and efficiency.
Feed or breeding-practice adoption does not directly measure enteric methane or parcel emissions.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025
facts: Defra provides annual UK agriculture statistics covering land, livestock, crops, inputs and environment.
National agricultural activity aggregates are not parcel emissions observations.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 summary
facts: The summary combines production, input and agri-environment indicators for 2025/2024 vintages.
Mixed-vintage headline indicators must retain their referenced year and scope.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 2 structure of industry
facts: The chapter reports agricultural area, crop area and livestock population aggregates.
Land area or animal counts are activity drivers, not direct GHG measurements.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 5 productivity
facts: The chapter reports Total Factor Productivity and input/output volume indices; 2025 figures are provisional.
Productivity change is economic/production performance and not measured GHG intensity unless an explicit emissions numerator is supplied.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 7 crops
facts: The chapter reports crop area, yield and production across major crops.
Crop production and yield are activity data and do not directly establish soil or fertiliser emissions.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 8 livestock
facts: The chapter reports livestock populations, slaughter and meat/milk/egg production and includes a correction to milk value.
Animal population and production volumes are activity data, not direct methane or nitrous-oxide measurements.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 9 intermediate consumption
facts: The chapter reports agricultural feed, energy, fertiliser and other input costs/indices.
Input expenditure or price is not physical activity or emissions without quantity and method evidence.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 11 agri-environment
facts: The chapter reports estimated agricultural GHG and air-pollution emissions plus fertiliser use and soil nutrient balances.
National sector estimates are not farm or parcel measurements.

sources.title: Agriculture in the United Kingdom 2025 chapter 12 organics
facts: The chapter reports organic land, land use, livestock and operator statistics.
Organic certification/status does not itself quantify GHG emissions or removals.

sources.title: British Survey of Fertiliser Practice 2025 annual report
facts: Defra publishes accredited annual fertiliser-practice statistics for Great Britain.
Fertiliser application practice/quantity requires gas-specific inventory methods before N2O inference and is not parcel-bound automatically.

sources.title: British survey of fertiliser practice dataset
facts: The dataset page provides 2025 report tables, extended time series and machine-readable data.
Dataset values retain survey scope, crop/grassland categories, units and year; they are not direct GHG observations.

sources.title: Monthly UK cattle sheep and pig slaughter and meat production data to June 2026
facts: Defra reports monthly slaughter counts, carcase weights and meat production.
Slaughter and production are activity data and cannot be treated as direct enteric/manure GHG emissions.

sources.title: Provisional Woodland Statistics 2026 GOV.UK
facts: The release provides provisional woodland area, planting and Woodland Carbon Code uptake statistics.
Woodland area/project registration is not an observed carbon-removal amount for a parcel.

sources.title: Forest Research Provisional Woodland Statistics
facts: Forest Research corrected 2026 conifer/broadleaf figures and historical time series while total woodland area remained unchanged.
Corrections and woodland-area estimates must retain vintage; area change is not direct carbon-stock change.

sources.title: Forest Research forestry time series
facts: The time-series page provides woodland area, planting/restocking and Woodland Carbon Code project series with July 2026 corrections.
Project counts/areas and corrected series do not directly measure realised removals.

sources.title: Forestry Statistics 2025
facts: Forestry Statistics 2025 includes a dedicated carbon chapter plus woodland, timber and methodology chapters.
National forestry carbon statistics and methodology are not automatic cadastral parcel observations.

sources.title: ONS Woodland natural capital accounts UK 2026 release
facts: ONS publishes woodland extent and ecosystem-service natural-capital accounts.
Natural-capital ecosystem-service estimates and valuations are accounting outputs, not direct parcel GHG measurements.

sources.title: Woodland natural capital accounts UK 2026 GOV.UK
facts: The GOV.UK gateway identifies the ONS 2026 woodland natural-capital release.
Publication metadata and natural-capital accounting do not establish parcel carbon flux.

sources.title: ONS Woodland natural capital accounts UK summary tables
facts: The dataset provides detailed woodland natural-resource financial and societal-value tables.
Economic/social valuation is not a physical emissions/removals measurement.

sources.title: ONS Enclosed farmland natural capital accounts UK 2026
facts: ONS reports extent, condition and ecosystem services for enclosed farmland.
Natural-capital habitat accounting and ecosystem-service valuation are not direct farm GHG measurements.

sources.title: ONS UK habitat natural capital accounts quality and methods guide
facts: ONS documents quality and methodology for habitat natural-capital accounts.
Methodology provenance does not create a new physical carbon observation.

sources.title: UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions 2005 to 2024
facts: DESNZ publishes local-authority and regional GHG estimates based on national datasets and inventory methods.
Local-authority estimates are spatial aggregates and do not provide cadastral parcel emissions.

sources.title: 2005 to 2024 UK local and regional GHG statistical release web accessible
facts: The release describes local estimates, revisions and LULUCF sources/sinks, including local-authority reconciliation with the national inventory.
Area-level allocation and end-use distribution are modelled statistical allocation rather than parcel measurement.

sources.title: Mapping GHG emissions and removals for LULUCF 2005 to 2024
facts: The methodology covers forestry, peatland, cropland, grassland, settlements, bioenergy crops, uncertainties and recalculations.
Mapped/disaggregated LULUCF estimates are not exact cadastral parcel observations without validated parcel geometry and measurement linkage.

sources.title: UK greenhouse gas emissions local authority and regional National Data Library
facts: The National Data Library catalogue exposes the 2005 to 2024 local GHG CSV, technical report, LULUCF mapping and protected-landscape tables.
Catalogue/data access establishes provenance and aggregate geography, not parcel binding.

sources.title: UK Statistics on Waste National Data Library
facts: Defra waste statistics cover waste from households, biodegradable municipal waste to landfill, packaging, C&D, C&I, generation, treatment and infrastructure.
Waste tonnage/treatment statistics are activity data and do not directly quantify methane or parcel GHG emissions.
